name: Safed (Tzfat)
tagline: A hilltop town of blue-doored synagogues and artists' galleries, and for five centuries the centre of Kabbalah, the tradition of Jewish mysticism.
highlight: The Old Jewish Quarter's lanes, with their ancient synagogues, blue doors and views towards Mount Meron.
shortDescription: The highest city in Israel, a place of pilgrimage for Jewish mystical study, with an artists' quarter, cooler summers and views over the Galilee.
metaDescription: A Safed (Tzfat) travel guide: the Old Jewish Quarter and Kabbalah synagogues, the artists' quarter, Meron, klezmer and food, Shabbat, when to go and a one-day plan.
suggestedStay: Half a day to a day
nearestAirport: Tel Aviv Ben Gurion (TLV), about 2 hours 30 minutes
knownFor: Kabbalah, the Old Jewish Quarter, synagogues, artists' galleries, cool summers
goodFor: Jewish history and mysticism, art, walking, cooler summer days

image.alt: A stone lane in Safed's old city with blue doors and shutters

intro: Safed is one of the four holy cities of Judaism, along with Jerusalem, Hebron and Tiberias, and at about 900 metres it is the highest city in Israel. It sits on a ridge in the Upper Galilee, with views over the surrounding hills and, on a clear day, Mount Hermon and the Sea of Galilee. Its climate is cooler than the coast, and it has long been a summer retreat.

The town's fame comes from the 16th century, when Jews expelled from Spain settled here and it became a centre of Kabbalah, the mystical tradition of Judaism. Scholars such as Isaac Luria and Joseph Karo lived and taught in Safed, and Karo compiled the Shulchan Aruch, a major code of Jewish law. Their synagogues, named after them, are still in use.

Today the town is a mix of ultra-Orthodox and Hasidic communities, artists who moved to the old quarter after 1948, and visitors. Its atmosphere is relaxed in the day and very quiet on Shabbat. It is small, it takes only a few hours to see, and it is a good place for a day trip from the Sea of Galilee.

whyVisit.intro: Safed is worth visiting for its setting and its atmosphere, and even more if you are interested in Jewish history and thought.

points.title: A centre of Kabbalah
points.text: For centuries, scholars from around the world came here to study Jewish mysticism, and their synagogues and study houses still stand.

points.title: An atmospheric old quarter
points.text: Narrow stone lanes, blue-painted doors and shutters, courtyards and arched passages make the old city one of the most photogenic in Israel.

points.title: The artists' quarter
points.text: Painters, sculptors and jewellers have galleries and workshops in the old Arab quarter, and it is a good place to buy something original.

points.title: Cool air and views
points.text: At 900 m, Safed is cooler than the coast and the Jordan Valley, with views over the Galilee that are especially good in the evening.

points.title: Close to the Sea of Galilee
points.text: The lake is about 30 minutes away, so Safed makes an easy add-on to a Galilee trip.

attractionsIntro: Safed's sights are within a few minutes' walk of each other, and the town can be seen in a morning or afternoon.

attractions.name: The Old Jewish Quarter
attractions.text: A network of lanes and stairs lined with synagogues, study houses and houses painted in shades of blue, a colour that is traditionally used to ward off the evil eye. It is a quiet and photogenic area.
attractions.tip: Go in the morning, and dress modestly.

attractions.name: The Ari Ashkenazi Synagogue
attractions.text: A synagogue named after Rabbi Isaac Luria, known as the Ari, the great 16th-century Kabbalist. It has an ornate Torah ark and a courtyard that overlooks the hills.
attractions.tip: Men should cover their heads, and women should dress modestly. Check the opening hours.

attractions.name: The Joseph Karo Synagogue
attractions.text: A synagogue named after Rabbi Joseph Karo, the author of the Shulchan Aruch. It stands next to his study house and has an atmospheric interior.
attractions.tip: It is one of the oldest in the town, and often quiet.

attractions.name: The Artists' Quarter
attractions.text: A neighbourhood of galleries and studios in the former Arab quarter, with an Ottoman-era mosque, a Khan and an art museum. The Safed Glass Museum and other small museums are nearby.
attractions.tip: Combine it with lunch or coffee.

attractions.name: The Citadel Park (Metzudat Tzfat)
attractions.text: A hilltop park with the ruins of a Crusader castle and views of the surrounding hills. It is the best place in town for a view.

attractions.name: The Ancient Cemetery
attractions.text: A hillside cemetery with the graves of Kabbalists and scholars, including Isaac Luria and Joseph Karo, painted in blue and white. It is a place of pilgrimage.

attractions.name: Meron
attractions.text: A village about 10 km away with the tomb of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, a great teacher in Jewish tradition, and a place of huge pilgrimages on Lag BaOmer in spring. The mountain and the village are also a nature reserve.
attractions.tip: It is very crowded on Lag BaOmer, and access is restricted on that day.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the old lanes
thingsToDo.text: Wander the stairs and arches of the Old Jewish Quarter and the artists' area, and stop for coffee.

thingsToDo.title: Visit the synagogues
thingsToDo.text: See the Ari, Karo and Abuhav synagogues, each with its own history and design.
thingsToDo.tip: Check the opening hours, as they vary, and dress modestly.

thingsToDo.title: Meet the artists
thingsToDo.text: Visit studios in the Artists' Quarter, where many painters and craftspeople work, and buy something to take home.
thingsToDo.tip: Studios are usually closed on Saturdays.

thingsToDo.title: Try a Kabbalah class or tour
thingsToDo.text: Several institutes offer introductory lectures and guided tours on Kabbalah and its history.

thingsToDo.title: Enjoy the Klezmer festival
thingsToDo.text: The Safed Klezmer Festival, held in summer, brings Jewish folk music to the streets and the old town.
thingsToDo.tip: Check dates, and book accommodation early.

thingsToDo.title: Visit Meron or hike in the Upper Galilee
thingsToDo.text: Mount Meron, the highest peak in Israel proper, has hiking trails and a nature reserve.

foodIntro: Safed's food is mostly kosher, and it is a good place to try local Galilee ingredients, cheeses and honey.

foods.name: Local cheese
foods.text: The Upper Galilee is known for goat and sheep cheeses, produced on small farms and sold in the town.
foods.whereToTry: Shops in the old city and farms nearby.

foods.name: Falafel and hummus
foods.text: Classic Israeli street food, available in the town centre.

foods.name: Fresh salads and dips
foods.text: Many restaurants serve a spread of salads with tahini, olives and bread.

foods.name: Galilee wine
foods.text: Wineries in the hills around Safed produce good wines, some of which are kosher.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants and wine shops in the town.

foods.name: Honey and sweets
foods.text: Honey, halva and dried fruit are sold in shops and markets.
foods.whereToTry: The main street and the old city.

foods.name: Shabbat meals
foods.text: Challah, fish and cholent are served at Shabbat meals, and some guesthouses open their tables to visitors.
foods.whereToTry: Guesthouses and synagogues that offer Shabbat hospitality.

accommodation.intro: Most visitors go as a day trip, but a night in Safed is quiet and atmospheric. Guesthouses are simple, and many are run by religious families.

areas.name: The old city
areas.text: Guesthouses and boutique hotels in restored old buildings, with views over the hills. They are quiet at night.

areas.name: The upper town
areas.text: Larger hotels along the ridge, with panoramic views and easier access by car.

gettingThere.intro: Safed is about 2.5 hours from Tel Aviv, and easiest by car or bus.

options.text: About 30–40 minutes from Tiberias and 1 hour 30 minutes from Haifa. The road climbs steeply, with views.
options.detail: Parking in the old city is limited.

options.text: Buses run to Safed from Tiberias, Haifa and Tel Aviv. The central bus station is a short taxi ride from the old city.
options.detail: Buses do not run on Shabbat.

options.text: Day tours of the north often include Safed, Nazareth and the Sea of Galilee.

gettingAround.intro: The old city is pedestrian and hilly.

options.text: The sights are within 10–15 minutes' walk, but the lanes are steep and there are many steps.
Taxis take you to the bus station, Meron and the upper town.
Useful for Meron and the area, but park outside the old city.

bestTime.headline: April–June and September–November
bestTime.summary: Safed's altitude makes it cooler than most of Israel, and summer is a popular season. Winters are cold and can bring snow.

seasons.text: Warm and green, with flowers on the hills. The best time for walking.
Warm and comfortable, often 25–30°C, and a popular getaway from the heat of the coast. It is busy with domestic tourists.
Clear and mild, with fewer visitors. The High Holidays affect opening hours.
Cold and often rainy or misty, sometimes with snow. Many guesthouses close.

bestTime.avoid: Shabbat, when almost everything is closed, and holiday weeks such as Lag BaOmer, when Meron is extremely crowded.

itinerary.title: One day in Safed
itinerary.intro: The old quarter and synagogues in the morning, the artists' quarter and lunch, and sunset at the citadel.

days.title: Kabbalah, art and views
days.summary: A slow day in a hill town.
days.morning: The Old Jewish Quarter and the Ari and Karo synagogues.
days.afternoon: The artists' quarter, lunch, and the ancient cemetery.

tipsIntro: Safed is small and traditional, and a few tips help.
tips: Avoid Shabbat unless you are staying for it. From Friday afternoon to Saturday evening, almost everything is closed, and driving in the old city is offensive to residents.
Dress modestly. Shoulders and knees should be covered, and women should wear long skirts in the synagogues.
Take a jacket in the evening and in the shoulder seasons, as it is cooler than the coast.
Check synagogue opening hours, which vary, and some are open only in the morning.
Ask before photographing people, especially religious residents.
Combine Safed with the Sea of Galilee, but do not rush it.
Follow local advice on security. The north has been affected by conflict, and Safed is near the northern border.

faq.a: It is one of Judaism's four holy cities and a centre of Kabbalah since the 16th century. It is also known for its artists' quarter, its cool climate and its picturesque old town.

faq.q: How long do you need in Safed?
faq.a: Half a day to a day. It is small, and you can see the main synagogues and the artists' quarter in a few hours.
A mystical tradition within Judaism that seeks to understand the nature of God and the universe. The best-known Kabbalists lived in Safed in the 16th century.
Most shops and restaurants close from Friday afternoon to Saturday evening. It is a beautiful time to visit if you want to experience a Shabbat in a religious town, but plan food and transport ahead.
It is generally regarded as safe, but it lies close to Israel's northern border, and the region has been affected by conflict. Check your government's advice.
Yes, for its atmosphere, views and history, and particularly if you are interested in Jewish religion and culture. It combines well with the Sea of Galilee.
